observation.visible_scene: A single large faceted transparent gemstone (pear/marquise-like cut) with blue-white iridescent internal reflections rests on a glossy black mirror surface, producing a clear inverted reflection directly beneath it. The backdrop is pure black dotted with a few tiny scattered light specks. The stone's outline and its position relative to the frame stay essentially fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: A bright starburst specular flare / lens-glare travels along the top edge of the stone: in the first frames it sits at the upper-right tip, then from around the middle of the clip it relocates to the upper-center-left ridge and grows into a taller, brighter vertical streak.
The colored facet highlights inside the gem (blue, violet, white bands) shift position and intensity from frame to frame, mirroring the same movement in the reflection below.
A handful of small white light points in the black background flicker and drift slightly in brightness/position.

The gemstone silhouette, its orientation, and the location of its mirror reflection do not translate or rotate; the visible motion is confined to the moving highlight and the shimmering internal reflections.
outside_clip_unknowns: What causes the highlight to move (a shifting light source, camera movement, or a post-production sparkle effect) is not determinable from the black background.
Whether the gem is being rotated on a turntable or held still is not shown; only the static silhouette is visible within this segment.
The start and end of the sparkle sequence lie outside the cropped frames.
uncertain_details: Camera versus light-source motion cannot be separated because the background is featureless.
The exact nature of the tiny background specks (dust, particles, or lens artifacts) is unclear.
Any micro-rotation of the stone is below the resolution of the silhouette, so the object is treated as stationary.
